expectations.text: B1: Scaffolds milestone 1 (init / repo layout) with TODOs for the learner and does not hand over the code for later milestones (objects, trees, commits)
expectations.evidence: Only milestone 1 was implemented: mygit.py docstring 'Step 1: `init` — create the .git directory skeleton' and 'Step one is done: mygit.py implements init'. No code for later milestones was handed over — step two is described in prose only ('Step two is the object model: implement `hash-object`... and `cat-file`... Say the word and we'll build it'), and mygit.py contains only the init command on the dispatch skeleton.

expectations.text: B2: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: a concrete command to run and the expected output/behaviour
expectations.evidence: Ends with a runnable checkpoint: 'Try it: `python3 mygit.py init myproject`, then poke around `.git/` and run real `git status` inside' with expected behaviour given — the annotated .git/ layout (HEAD → "ref: refs/heads/main") and 'real git accepts its output as a valid repo (`git status` → "On branch main / No commits yet")'.

expectations.text: B3: States that a repository needs .git/objects, .git/refs (heads) and a HEAD file pointing at refs/heads/<branch>
expectations.evidence: Layout diagram states all three: 'objects/{info,pack}/ ← empty; the object database lives here' plus 'objects/ is the database'; 'refs/{heads,tags}/ ← empty; branches will be files here'; and 'HEAD → "ref: refs/heads/main" (a pointer, not a hash)' with 'HEAD is a symbolic ref. It holds the *path* of a branch, and a branch is a file under refs/heads/'.

expectations.text: B4: Stays inside the workspace and does not run any install command (brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install); if tools are needed it asks the learner to install them
expectations.evidence: Recorded commands are only 'rm -rf test-repo && ls -la' and 'ls -la' — no install commands (no brew/apt/pip/cargo/rustup/npm -g/go install/gem install) and all executed commands are workspace-local. The out-of-workspace attempt was denied by the sandbox and wrote nothing ('The compound command hit a permission issue... Even `whoami` is denied'), after which the agent self-corrected: 'I'll test inside the workspace instead.' No tools needed installing; Python was already assumed per the prompt.
